### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**4** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them. ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/mcp/src/skill-md.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/mcp/src/skill-md.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **12** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 6a7403bae14c7db5f21ad4a214198616aecf15f2` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `5cfc18e74fda42094a6c2f57859c924b96715dab` — the merge of head `51462546a25ddeffb7577e1991b4d26edae88b44` into base `6a7403bae14c7db5f21ad4a214198616aecf15f2`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh

git fetch origin 5cfc18e74fda42094a6c2f57859c924b96715dab && git checkout 5cfc18e74fda42094a6c2f57859c924b96715dab
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 6a7403bae14c7db5f21ad4a214198616aecf15f2 51462546a25ddeffb7577e1991b4d26edae88b44 && git checkout -B drift-repro 6a7403bae14c7db5f21ad4a214198616aecf15f2 && git merge --no-ff 51462546a25ddeffb7577e1991b4d26edae88b44

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 6a7403bae14c7db5f21ad4a214198616aecf15f2

Head `dc4f0a0d0307fc5247afa35c3f455d84c5cbc7aa` is the first and final head. The dev report is 6927898657 on #34340.

- **The change.** The MCP `delete_record` tool description and its `confirm` member carry the same two sentences, defined once beside the registration. A request in which the human names the record to delete, with exactly one record matching, is the human's approval of that delete, so `confirm: true` is sent on that call. When the name matches more than one record, or the request does not identify one record, the agent lists the candidates and asks first. The gate itself is unchanged: 428 `ACTION_CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED` without `confirm: true`. The recycle-bin sentence and `delete_records` (bulk) are also unchanged.
- **Pins.** Both sentences are pinned verbatim on the description and on the member as `tools/list` serves them. A control pins that `delete_records` carries neither. The existing gate pins stay green. An ablation of the member sentence went red (1 failed, 10 passed), and the HEAD blob was restored.
- **Readings.** `@objectstack/mcp` test: 66 files and 1225 tests pass. Typecheck: exit 0. Dispatch gates: 68 derived, 67 run with exit 0, and 1 not measured. The one not measured is `check:dual-build-cjs-loads`, which exited 3 on its prerequisite because only the mcp closure was built.
- **CI on this head:** 35 success, 16 skipped, 0 failed.
- **Tier:** not governed, 96 lines. `Clause-②: no`, `Metadata-protocol: none`.
- **Skills-docs:** the follow-up is filed as #34456 (`skills/objectstack-ai/SKILL.md`, plus the same family outside `skills/**`). The body line now names it.
- **Owed:** the L1 review (L1-a).

## 席位核对 · REWORK (L1, first read) · Head-sha: dc4f0a0d0307fc5247afa35c3f455d84c5cbc7aa · 2026-11-16T20:15Z

L1 thread L1-a for area o1-A, reading the final head named in 6927980065 against the dev report 6927898657 and card #34340 (p1, the maintainer's ruling 「点名单条就算确认」 quoted on the card). The diff has 3 files, +92/−4.

### What holds

- **The tool text.** The two sentences match the card's item 1 and the ruling: a request naming one record with exactly one match is the approval, and ambiguity or no identified record means asking first. They are defined once and used on both the `delete_record` description and its `confirm` member. The description drops only "ask the human first, then retry" and keeps the gate sentence, the recycle-bin fact and the `recycleBinEntryId` sentence.
- **The gate is unchanged.** `recordDeleteConfirmationRefusal` is untouched, and the existing describe still pins 428 `ACTION_CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED` with the engine's `delete` never called. The old assertion `toMatch(/ask the human/i)` still holds against the new text ("ask the human which one"). Only its comment changed.
- **`delete_records` (bulk) is unchanged** (item 2), and the control test pins that neither sentence reaches it.
- **The pin and its ablation.** The new describe pins both sentences verbatim on both surfaces as `tools/list` serves them. The recorded ablation turned it red.
- **The changeset** is `@objectstack/mcp: patch` with `Clause-②: no` and `Metadata-protocol: none`. Each sentence matches the code.
- **Item 3, the `skills/**` row**, goes to #34456 (`domain:skills`, p2, `pm:blocked`), and the PR body names it. That split is right: `skills/**` is outside an implementation card's file surface.

### Must fix

- **M1. The MCP server's own served skill still tells the agent to ask first for every `delete_record`.**
  - *Where.* `packages/mcp/src/skill-md.ts` is the text the same server serves at `GET /api/v1/mcp/skill`. Lines 455–458 still say "Ask your human first; the flag asserts an approval, it does not obtain one."
  - *Why it blocks.* After this PR, one server hands an agent two instructions that disagree: the tool description says a named single match is the approval, and the served skill says to ask first. That is the same two-way reading the card exists to remove: 76 of 121 failed in-chat writes came from it, and every model has to act the same way.
  - *Why it belongs here.* This is not the `skills/**` path that #34456 holds. It is a non-governed source file in the package this PR already edits, so it is inside this card's reach.
  - *What closes it.*
    - The `delete_record` bullet (455–458) states the same rule. Interpolating the two constants from `mcp-http-tools.ts` keeps them from drifting apart, since `skill-md.ts` already imports from there.
    - The gotcha at 528 ("Confirm destructive actions (`delete_record`, …) with the user") and the workflow step at 550 ("confirming destructive steps with the user") get a qualifier: a delete the human named, with one match, is already confirmed.
    - One assertion on the served skill text pins it.
  - *What it touches.* Nothing on the contract faces, so it stays L1-only.

### Should (this round, or on #34456 if the seat prefers)

- **S1.** `content/docs/ai/connect-mcp.mdx`, around lines 628–632, says "The agent asks its human, then retries" and still calls an MCP record delete "permanent", although a business record goes to the recycle bin (#33692). #34456 lists it as "same family, outside `skills/**`", but a `domain:skills` card is the wrong holder for a `content/docs` page. It either rides this PR's fix round, or the seat names its holder on #34456.

### Note (not blocking)

- **N1.** The refusal message of the gate (`mcp-http-tools.ts:1217`, "confirm with the human in the loop, then retry this call") is reached only without `confirm: true`. That still includes an agent that forgot the member on a delete the human named, which is then told to ask again. Saying "send `confirm: true` once the human has approved, which a request naming exactly one record already is" would align it. It is the seat's call, since it changes a pinned refusal text.
- **N2.** The dev's open question about the signed HTML trailer in the `pr_create` body and the os-dev.md exception list concerns governed text (`.claude/**`) and is the seat's, not L1's. It has no effect on this verdict.

### Checks and landing

- **Checks on this head** (check-runs): 55 runs. 36 success, 18 skipped, 1 still running, 0 failed.
- **Base.** The merge base is `6aeb665f`, and K = 3. `git merge-tree` against current main is clean, per the dev report and my own read of the base.
- **L2.** None owed: no `packages/spec/src/**`, no governed path, `Clause-②: no`, and no narrowing. The tool-description text is checked at L1 sentence by sentence, as above.
- **Landing.** Not Tier H. After M1, area o1-A lands it.

所以失败的测试可能在本 PR 没碰过的包里 —— 那不是重排能修的。每次盲目重排都会让排在后面的所有 PR 重建一轮。

**分类：`failure`** —— 按下面的日志分诊。

**失败的 job（日志抽取，best effort）：**

    ↳ 失败原因: @objectstack/dogfood:test: AssertionError: expected { mode: 'inline', inserted: +0, …(5) } to match object { mode: 'inline', inserted: 28 }
  ```

> `↳ 失败原因` 是判读的关键：**超时**（`Test timed out in …` / `Hook timed out in …`）多半是负载/时序，不是本 PR 的回归；
> **断言**（`AssertionError: …`）才指向真实的行为改变。两者的 `FAIL` 行长得一模一样，只有这一行能区分。
>
> ⚠️ **断言这一侧有一类例外，判据是断言在测什么，不是它是不是 `AssertionError`。** 断言的对象是**产品行为**（一个值、一个形状、一次拒收）⇒ 照上面读：真实的行为改变，去查，⛔ 不要重排掉；
> 断言的对象是**这次实验自身的有效性前提**（跑完的耗时、负载下的先后、任何只在时间预算内才成立的条件）⇒ 它跟**超时**是同一类，同样对负载敏感，重排一次是合法的判别手段。
> 识别是机械的：断言的消息或它比较的值本身点名了一段**时长、一个时间戳、一个耗时计数**。实测过的一对 —— `AssertionError: SecurityPlugin.init() ran: expected false to be true` 测的是产品行为（真回归）；
> `AssertionError: this run took over a second, so second-precision stamps could have differed too: expected 1006 to be less than 1000` 测的是实验前提：它守护的那条不变式当时是绿的，同一个 head 原样重排一次即成功。
> 穿着 `AssertionError` 外衣的时间测量，仍然是时间测量。（⛔ 这只改「怎么读一次红」，不改「哪些测试可以重排」——后者由别处管。）
